races.title: State Assembly, District 15
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Anamarie Avila Farias
cands.bio: Democratic member of the California State Assembly for District 15 since December 2024. Previously on the Martinez City Council (elected 2012), the Contra Costa County Board of Education, and the California Housing Finance Agency board. Holds degrees from the University of San Francisco.

endorsements.text: Democratic Party of California, California Federation of Labor Unions (AFL-CIO), IUOE Local 3, and the National Union of Healthcare Workers endorsed her in 2026.
Equality California and California Young Democrats are listed among her 2026 endorsements and voter guide recommendations.

cands.gaps: We found no documented statements or actions by her on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, growth limits, school choice, abortion, gun policy or police pay. The Ballotpedia list of bills she sponsored was empty on the page we read, so we could not confirm her authored bills beyond the one reported by Wikipedia. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2024 or 2026. We found no news reporting on controversies. A 2022 Facebook post about boycotting the 4th of July appears only on Wikipedia, so we left it out.

local.label: Roots 100: Wikipedia says she was born in Martinez, California, and her campaign site calls her a lifelong, third-generation Contra Costa County resident who grew up in her hometown of Martinez.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Assemblymember since December 2024. Earlier she served on the Martinez City Council (2012), the Contra Costa County Board of Education (elected 2020) and the California Housing Finance Agency board (appointed 2015, reappointed 2021). Her campaign site says she chaired and served on the Martinez Planning Commission for nearly a decade.
qual.why: She holds a sitting legislative office and has prior local elected service. She also has housing-finance and policy experience, which fits a job of writing law and the state budget.

workers-first.evidence: Introduced a bill in January 2026 to bar people employed by ICE between September 2025 and January 2029 from working in law enforcement or the public school system in California.

cands.name: Arthur Webb
cands.bio: Technology professional and a University of California, Berkeley graduate (1971). Ran for California State Assembly District 15 in 2026 as a No Party Preference candidate. Describes himself as a moderate independent. Has not held public office, according to the sources read.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists Reform California among his endorsements and voter-guide recommendations.
Ballotpedia lists The Morning Answer with Jennifer Horn among his endorsements and voter-guide recommendations.
Ballotpedia lists three voter guides among his recommendations: April's Common Sense Cali Voters, Based in Malibu, and Elizabeth Barcohana's Lady with a Brain Voter Guide.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Arthur Webb was born or raised, or when he moved to California. Ballotpedia names Redlands High School and UC Berkeley (1971), but nothing confirms his upbringing. His employers and years of work as a technology professional are not described, and neither is any business he has owned. He has held no public office, so there are no votes or official actions to report. We did not find any stated positions from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, immigration or H-1B, policing, guns, abortion, or school choice. The 'Meet Arthur' biography page was not available, and the campaign Issues page was cut off partway through.
